Subject: Re: [Redwood] Interactive conversation throughput spike

Hi Samir —

Thanks for flagging this. We detected a spike in interactive response latency affecting streaming endpoints starting ~10:05 PDT this morning and are actively investigating. I wanted to confirm what we're seeing on your side and share short-term mitigations we can apply immediately.

What we know so far:
- Impact: intermittent slow token cadence / pauses in streaming for ~10–30s for a subset of sessions (estimated ~3% of BrightCart requests).
- Window: began ~10:05 PDT, highest severity between 10:10–10:35.
- Symptoms: stalled chunks, perceived slow typing, occasional reconnects.

Immediate actions we are taking:
1) Rerouting a portion of BrightCart streaming traffic to a warmed fallback pool that disables continuous batching for affected model family. This will slightly increase token cost but should restore steady chunk delivery.
2) Increasing KV-cache warmup priority for your model instances to reduce cold-KV stalls.
3) Capturing request-level traces; can you please send a short HAR or trace from an affected session? That helps correlate on ingress.

Short customer playbook (quick workarounds you can apply now):
- Increase client stream timeout to 45s and enable automatic chunk reconnection (backoff 1s, max tries 3).
- Use non-streaming generation for critical checkout flows until we confirm full recovery.
- If possible, pin to model variant rdl-3b-v1 which we are warming as a fallback.

I will keep you posted every 30 minutes or sooner. Diego (ENG) is on this and Monica (CS) is coordinating the support delivery. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts live chat and checkout interactions.

Best,
Avery

Subject: RE: Fwd: BrightCart - streaming stalls (customer-facing) — triage results and mitigation

Quick update from ENG triage:

Findings (root cause):
- Trigger: a transient autoscaler oscillation in the us-west-2 serving pool caused a subset of model shards to be rebalanced while some long-running streaming sessions had KV caches not fully populated.
- Effect: requests routed to shards with cold KV entries experienced token scheduling stalls during KV fetch/population; continuous batching exacerbated perceived pause (several requests were waiting for the same KV fetch).
- Scope: impacted ~3–4% of streaming connections for BrightCart during peak window. No model corruption; no data exfiltration.

Immediate mitigations executed (12:05–12:30 PDT):
- Forced traffic reroute for BrightCart to a warmed fallback pool (disabled continuous batch coalescing for the pool).
- Increased KV-cache refill concurrency for the affected shard set.
- Added a temporary rule to prefer shards with warm KV for pinned-customer requests.

Customer guidance (what to do on your side):
- Short-term: switch critical checkout flows to non-streaming generation for 30–60 minutes if you need guaranteed token delivery without pause. Expect slightly higher end-to-end latency (300–500ms larger tail depending on prompt length) but consistent completion semantics.
- Recommended client config if staying on streaming: increase per-stream timeout to 45s, enable reconnection with jittered backoff (1s/2s/4s), and implement idempotent continuation by resending the last chunk token index on reconnect.

Planned follow-ups (engineering):
- We will add a serving-level preference to avoid rebalancing live streaming sessions during autoscale windows (ETA 3 weeks for a safe rollout).
- Improve pre-warm heuristics for customer-pinned shards (ETA 2 weeks).
- Postmortem and public incident summary to be delivered by EOD tomorrow (Apr 28).

I'll join BrightCart's channel at 12:45 to walk through any traces they have.

Diego

Subject: Post-incident update: April 27 — streaming stalls affecting BrightCart (summary + action items)

Samir —

Thank you again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary, actions we've taken, and recommended mitigations for BrightCart. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute review call today to walk through the technical details.

Summary / timeline
- 10:05 PDT: First telemetry shows rise in token scheduling latency for a subset of streaming sessions.
- 10:10–10:35 PDT: Peak user impact; customer reports stalled chunks (~12–18s pauses).
- 10:25 PDT: SR opened, HAR received from BrightCart.
- 12:05–12:30 PDT: Engineering executed traffic reroute to warmed fallback pool and increased KV-cache concurrency. Observed steady recovery afterward.

Root cause
- An autoscaler rebalancing event moved some shards while long-lived streaming sessions had cold KV caches. Cold KV population + continuous batching produced token scheduling stalls for impacted sessions.

Actions taken for BrightCart (done)
- Rerouted your traffic to a warmed fallback pool (reduces stalls).
- Increased KV-cache refill concurrency on affected shards.
- Disabled continuous batching on the fallback pool to avoid coalesced stalls.

Actions we will take (committed)
- Serving change to avoid shard rebalancing for live streaming sessions (ETA ~3 weeks).
- Better pre-warm heuristics for pinned customers (ETA ~2 weeks).
- Post-incident monitoring alert tuned to detect similar KV-population stalls earlier.

Customer mitigations (recommended)
- Use non-streaming generation for critical checkout flows for the next 48 hours if you require deterministic completion semantics.
- If continuing streaming: set stream timeout = 45s and implement reconnection with idempotent resumption.

Compensation and next steps
- Laura (cc'd) will follow up with compensation options for the impacted window (possible service credit).
- We can run a joint load test in a dedicated window to validate the upgraded warmup heuristics once rolled out.

Apology
- We know this affected your live user experience and are sorry for the disruption. We appreciate your help diagnosing this quickly and the HAR you provided was extremely valuable.

If you'd like to go deeper on the technical postmortem, Diego and I are available for a call this afternoon.

Best,
Avery
